3862991.formatting: Write in paragraph form or use bullet points for each management measure. Do not disclose the nature of the financial interest itself. Reference attachments if the plan is provided separately.

3862993.name: IRB/HRPP Contact Info (Multi-Site Reviewing)
3862993.prompt: Provide the IRB or Human Research Protection Program (HRPP) contact information for each participating site. Include the contact person's full name, title, and email address. This information is needed to facilitate communication between the reviewing IRB (TCU) and the relying institutions for reliance agreement coordination and ongoing oversight.
commonIssues: Providing only a generic departmental email instead of a specific contact person
Omitting the title or role of the IRB/HRPP contact
Not providing contact information for every participating site
Listing outdated contact information
Confusing the site PI contact with the IRB/HRPP office contact
Using acronyms for institutional names without spelling them out
3862993.formatting: Use a numbered list organized by site. For each site, provide the institution name, contact name, title, and email address on separate lines or in a structured format.

3863006.name: Reviewing Site IRB Contact (Multi-Site Relying)
3863006.prompt: Provide the IRB or HRPP contact information for the reviewing site (the institution whose IRB will serve as the IRB of Record for this study). Include the contact person's full name, title, and email address. This information enables the TCU IRB to coordinate the reliance agreement and communicate about protocol changes, reportable events, and ongoing oversight requirements.
commonIssues: Providing only a generic office email without a specific contact name
Omitting the contact person's title or role within the IRB/HRPP
Confusing the reviewing site PI with the reviewing site IRB administrator
Not providing a direct email for the IRB office or designated contact
Listing information for the wrong institution (e.g., the relying site instead of the reviewing site)
3863006.formatting: Provide the information in a structured format: contact name, title, institutional affiliation, and email address. Use complete institutional names without acronyms.

3863021.name: Study Activities Description (Multi-Site Relying)
3863021.prompt: Provide a detailed description of the specific study activities that will be conducted at TCU as a relying site. Expand on the activities you selected in the checklist by describing how each activity will be carried out, who will perform it, the timeline, and where at TCU it will occur. Be specific about which portions of the overall study protocol TCU personnel are responsible for versus what is handled by the reviewing site.
commonIssues: Repeating the checklist selections without adding meaningful procedural detail
Not specifying who at TCU will perform each activity
Failing to distinguish between activities performed at TCU versus those at other sites
Omitting the timeline or sequence of study activities at TCU
Not describing how TCU activities integrate with the broader multi-site protocol
Providing a copy of the full study protocol instead of focusing on TCU-specific activities
3863021.formatting: Write in paragraph form or use a numbered list organized by activity type. Clearly identify each activity, the responsible personnel, location, and timeline.

3863024.name: Who Conducts Data Analysis (Collaborative Research)
3863024.prompt: Identify all non-TCU individuals or groups who will conduct data analysis for this study. For each external analyst, provide their full name, institutional affiliation, and role in the analysis. You do not need to list TCU study team members. Specify whether the external collaborators will have access to identifiable data or only de-identified datasets, and describe any data use agreements that govern their access.
commonIssues: Listing TCU team members when the field asks only for non-TCU analysts
Providing institutional names without specific individual names and roles
Not specifying whether the external analyst will receive identifiable or de-identified data
Omitting mention of data use agreements or IRB approvals at the collaborator's institution
Failing to describe the collaborator's qualifications or expertise relevant to the analysis
Not addressing whether the collaborator's institution has its own IRB approval for this work
3863024.formatting: Use a structured format listing each external collaborator with their name, institution, role, and data access level. Write in complete sentences.

3863025.name: What Data Sent for Analysis (Collaborative Research)
3863025.prompt: Specify exactly what collected data will be sent to external collaborators for analysis. Identify each data type (e.g., survey responses, interview transcripts, biological specimen results, imaging data) and whether the data will be identifiable, coded, or fully de-identified before being sent. Describe any data transformations or de-identification steps that will occur before sharing.
commonIssues: Providing only a vague description like 'study data' without specifying data types
Not clarifying whether data will be de-identified, coded, or sent with identifiers
Omitting mention of who performs the de-identification before data transfer
Failing to address whether a code key will be shared with the external collaborator
Not describing all data types being shared (e.g., mentioning survey data but omitting demographic data)
Not addressing whether biological specimens themselves will be shipped versus only results
3863025.formatting: Use a bulleted list of each data type being shared, followed by its identification status (identifiable, coded, or de-identified). Describe de-identification steps in a separate paragraph.

3863030.name: Data Sharing with Collaborators (Collaborative Research)
3863030.prompt: Describe the method by which data will be transmitted to external collaborators and how the collaborator will store the data upon receipt. Specify the transfer mechanism (e.g., encrypted email, secure file transfer protocol, institutional cloud platform), the encryption or security measures during transit, and the storage environment at the collaborator's site (e.g., password-protected server, institutional secure drive, encrypted local device).
commonIssues: Stating data will be 'emailed' without specifying encryption or security measures
Not describing the storage environment at the receiving institution
Omitting details about access controls at the collaborator's site
Failing to mention whether institutional-approved platforms will be used versus personal devices
Not addressing data security during transit versus at rest separately
Providing vague statements like 'data will be shared securely' without specific mechanisms
3863030.formatting: Write in paragraph form. Address both the transfer method and the storage plan separately. Name specific platforms, tools, or protocols used.

3863031.name: Data Disposition After Analysis (Collaborative Research)
3863031.prompt: Describe what will happen to the data once the external collaborator completes their analysis. Specify whether the data will be returned to TCU, destroyed at the collaborator's site, or retained for a defined period. If data will be destroyed, describe the destruction method (e.g., secure deletion, certificate of destruction). If data will be retained, explain the retention period, justification, and ongoing security measures.
commonIssues: Not specifying a concrete plan for data disposition (return, destroy, or retain)
Failing to describe the method of destruction if data will be destroyed
Omitting a timeline for when data disposition will occur after analysis is complete
Not addressing whether a certificate of destruction or confirmation will be provided
Providing conflicting information between this field and the data management plan
Not addressing what happens to backup copies of the data at the collaborator's site
3863031.formatting: Write in paragraph form. Clearly state the disposition action (return, destroy, or retain), the timeline, the method, and any confirmation procedures.

3863035.name: Local Context - Political/Legal/Cultural (International Research)
3863035.prompt: Describe the political, legal, and cultural considerations specific to the international research location that are relevant to conducting your study. Address the current political stability, any laws or regulations that affect research with human subjects (e.g., data privacy laws, restrictions on certain research topics), cultural norms around consent and autonomy, and any power dynamics or vulnerabilities that may affect participant willingness to participate freely. Demonstrate familiarity with the local research environment.
commonIssues: Providing only a superficial or tourism-level description of the country without research-relevant details
Not addressing local data privacy or research ethics laws that may differ from U.S. regulations
Failing to discuss political stability or security considerations that could affect participants or researchers
Omitting cultural norms around informed consent, authority, or gender that affect voluntary participation
Not acknowledging power differentials between foreign researchers and local participants
Failing to address language barriers and their implications for informed consent
3863035.formatting: Write in paragraph form organized by category: political considerations, legal framework, and cultural factors. Cite specific laws or cultural practices where possible.

3863036.name: Scientific/Ethical Justification for International Setting
3863036.prompt: Explain why this research must be conducted in an international setting rather than domestically. Provide the scientific rationale (e.g., the study population, phenomenon, or condition is specific to that location) and the ethical justification (e.g., the research will benefit the local community, addresses a local health disparity, or involves a condition prevalent in that region). Address how the research avoids exploitation of the local population.
commonIssues: Not providing a scientific reason specific to the international location
Failing to explain why the research could not be conducted domestically
Omitting the ethical dimension of how the research benefits the local community
Providing only convenience-based justifications (e.g., existing collaborator, lower costs) without scientific rationale
Not addressing the concern of exploitation or 'helicopter research'
Failing to describe how findings will be shared with or benefit the international community
3863036.formatting: Write in paragraph form with clearly separated scientific and ethical justifications. Be specific about what makes the international setting essential.

3863037.name: Societal/Cultural Beliefs Impact on Research
3863037.prompt: Describe the societal and cultural beliefs in the research country that may impact how the research is conducted or that could alter the risks or benefits to participants. Address beliefs about research participation, medical treatment, bodily autonomy, privacy, gender roles, authority, or any stigmatized conditions relevant to your study. Explain how your study design accounts for these beliefs to minimize risk and respect local customs.
commonIssues: Providing a generic cultural overview without connecting it to specific study risks or procedures
Not addressing how cultural beliefs might affect informed consent or willingness to participate
Failing to discuss stigma associated with the research topic in the local culture
Omitting how gender norms or power dynamics might affect recruitment or data collection
Not explaining study design modifications made to respect local cultural practices
Assuming Western research norms apply universally without addressing cultural differences
3863037.formatting: Write in paragraph form. For each cultural factor identified, explain its relevance to your specific study and the mitigation or adaptation strategy you will employ.

3863040.name: International Risks and Mitigation
3863040.prompt: Describe the risks specific to conducting research internationally and the steps you will take to minimize them. Address risks to both participants and researchers, including political instability, travel safety, communication barriers, limited access to emergency services, data security across borders, potential for government surveillance, and any risks arising from the specific research topic in the local context. For each identified risk, provide a concrete mitigation strategy.
commonIssues: Listing risks without corresponding mitigation strategies
Not addressing risks to both participants and researchers
Omitting data security risks related to cross-border data transfer or local government access
Failing to address travel safety or emergency protocols for research personnel
Not considering the risk of participants being identified in small or close-knit communities
Providing only generic risk statements without connection to the specific study location
3863040.formatting: Use a structured format pairing each risk with its mitigation strategy. A table or paired bullet points work well. Address participant risks and researcher risks separately.

3863045.name: Culturally Appropriate Access (International Research)
3863045.prompt: Describe how the researcher will have culturally appropriate access to the community where the international research will be conducted. Explain existing relationships with local organizations, community leaders, or institutions that facilitate trust and access. Describe the researcher's familiarity with the local culture and language, any local collaborators or cultural liaisons who will assist, and how the research team will navigate cultural protocols for entering and working within the community.
commonIssues: Claiming cultural competence without providing evidence of prior experience or relationships
Not identifying specific local collaborators, organizations, or gatekeepers who will facilitate access
Failing to address language proficiency or plans for interpretation and translation
Omitting how community trust will be established before or during data collection
Not describing any formal community engagement or approval processes required locally
Providing only the name of a collaborating institution without explaining the relationship
3863045.formatting: Write in paragraph form. Name specific individuals, organizations, or community leaders involved. Describe the history of the relationship and the access strategy.

3863049.name: Local IRB/Ethics Committee Contact (International Research)
3863049.prompt: Provide the contact information for the local IRB or Ethics Committee equivalent at the international research location. Include the committee name, contact person's full name and title, institutional affiliation, mailing address, phone number, and email address. If the country does not have a formal IRB equivalent, explain the local ethical review process and identify the responsible authority.
commonIssues: Providing incomplete contact information (e.g., email only without name or title)
Not specifying the official name of the local ethics review body
Failing to verify that the committee is currently active and has jurisdiction over the proposed research
Omitting the country or city where the committee is located
Confusing a local collaborator's departmental review with the national or institutional ethics committee
Not addressing the situation when no formal IRB equivalent exists in the country
3863049.formatting: Present contact information in a structured format: committee name, contact person name, title, institution, address, phone, and email. Each element should be on its own line.

3863053.name: International - Please Describe (Other Considerations)
3863053.prompt: Describe any additional international research considerations not covered by the other fields in this section. This may include unique regulatory requirements, import/export restrictions on data or materials, visa or research permit requirements, local institutional approvals needed, or any other country-specific factors that the IRB should be aware of when reviewing this protocol.
commonIssues: Leaving this field blank when there are relevant considerations not addressed elsewhere
Repeating information already provided in other international research fields
Not mentioning research visa or permit requirements when applicable
Failing to address import/export restrictions on biological samples or research equipment
Omitting local institutional approvals or governmental research permits that are required
Not addressing customs or shipping regulations for research materials
3863053.formatting: Write in paragraph form. Clearly label each additional consideration and provide sufficient detail for the IRB to assess its impact on the study.

3863056.name: Communication with TCU IRB Internationally
3863056.prompt: Describe how researchers collecting data at the international site will communicate with the TCU IRB in the event the project requires changes, unanticipated problems arise, or there are reportable incidents. Specify the communication method (e.g., email, phone, video conference), expected response times given time zone differences, who will be responsible for reporting, and any backup communication plans if primary methods are unavailable due to local infrastructure limitations.
commonIssues: Providing only 'we will email the IRB' without addressing time zone or connectivity challenges
Not designating a specific person responsible for IRB communication from the international site
Failing to address what happens if internet or phone service is unreliable at the research location
Not describing the process for reporting unanticipated problems or adverse events
Omitting a timeline for reporting events (e.g., within 24 hours, within 5 business days)
Not addressing how urgent versus routine communications will be handled differently
3863056.formatting: Write in paragraph form. Address routine communications, urgent/reportable event communications, and backup communication methods as distinct topics.

3863057.name: Local Language Contact (International Research)
3863057.prompt: Identify a local contact who is fluent in the local language at the international research site and provide their full contact information. Include the contact's name, role in the study or relationship to the research team, language(s) spoken, institution or organization, phone number, and email address. This person should be able to assist with participant communication, translation needs, and serve as a local point of contact for the TCU IRB if needed.
commonIssues: Not providing complete contact information (name, phone, email, and affiliation)
Failing to specify which language(s) the contact speaks
Not explaining the contact's role or relationship to the research team
Listing someone who is not actually located at or near the research site
Omitting whether this person will assist with consent processes or participant questions
Not addressing the contact's availability during the data collection period
3863057.formatting: Present contact information in a structured format: name, role/relationship, languages spoken, institutional affiliation, phone number, and email address.

3863061.name: Costs to Participants
3863061.prompt: Describe all costs that participants may incur as a result of participating in this study, including direct costs (e.g., parking, transportation, medical procedures not covered by insurance) and indirect costs (e.g., time away from work, childcare). If there are no costs to participants, state this explicitly. If costs exist, explain whether participants will be reimbursed and how, and ensure the consent document accurately reflects these costs.
commonIssues: Failing to consider indirect costs such as transportation, parking, or lost wages
Not explicitly stating 'no costs to participants' when applicable, leaving the field vague
Omitting costs associated with study-related medical procedures or tests that are not standard of care
Not addressing whether insurance will be billed for any study-related procedures
Failing to describe reimbursement plans for participant-incurred expenses
Not ensuring the cost description matches what is stated in the consent document
3863061.formatting: List all potential costs clearly. If no costs exist, provide an explicit statement. Ensure consistency with the informed consent document.

3863065.name: Compensation Details
3863065.prompt: Describe in detail all forms of compensation (monetary and non-monetary) that participants will receive, including the specific amount or value, the form of payment (cash, gift card, course credit, SONA credit, etc.), and the schedule of payments. Address whether compensation will be prorated for participants who withdraw early or cannot complete all study procedures. If using a raffle or drawing, describe the selection method (e.g., every 5th participant) -- compensation cannot be purely random. Ensure the compensation is not so large as to constitute undue inducement.
commonIssues: Not specifying the exact dollar amount or value of non-monetary compensation
Failing to describe the proration schedule for participants who withdraw early
Using random raffle selection without describing the systematic method for choosing winners
Not addressing whether compensation could constitute undue inducement for the study population
Omitting the timing and method of compensation delivery
Failing to ensure compensation details in this section match the consent document exactly
3863065.formatting: Specify the type, amount, form, and timing of all compensation. If using prorated or milestone-based payments, include a clear schedule. Address early withdrawal compensation explicitly.

3863068.name: Potential Risks and Mechanisms to Reduce Risk
3863068.prompt: Identify all foreseeable risks to participants, including physical, psychological, social, economic, and legal risks, no matter how unlikely. For each risk, describe the likelihood and severity, and specify the concrete mechanisms or procedures that will be implemented to minimize that risk. Address risks from all study procedures (surveys, interviews, interventions, biological specimen collection, etc.). Include provisions for monitoring participant safety during the study and describe any stopping rules or referral procedures for participants who experience adverse events.
commonIssues: Listing only physical risks while ignoring psychological, social, economic, or legal risks
Stating that risks are 'minimal' without describing the specific risks and their mitigation
Failing to match risk descriptions to the specific procedures described in the study protocol
Not including a referral plan or resources for participants who experience emotional distress
Omitting monitoring procedures or stopping rules for detecting and responding to adverse events
Providing generic risk reduction statements without tying them to specific study procedures
3863068.formatting: Organize by risk category (physical, psychological, social, economic, legal). For each risk, state the risk, its likelihood and severity, and the specific mitigation strategy. Use a systematic, comprehensive approach.

3863069.name: Potential Benefits
3863069.prompt: Describe the potential benefits of the research, distinguishing clearly between direct benefits to individual participants and broader benefits to society or the field of knowledge. Do not list compensation as a benefit. If there are no direct benefits to participants, state this explicitly and describe only the anticipated contributions to generalizable knowledge. Do not overstate benefits or create therapeutic misconception.
commonIssues: Listing compensation or payment as a benefit of the research
Overstating direct benefits to individual participants, creating therapeutic misconception
Failing to distinguish between direct benefits to participants and benefits to society or science
Not explicitly stating when there are no direct benefits to participants
Providing vague societal benefits without connecting them to the study's specific contributions
Claiming definitive outcomes (e.g., 'participants will improve') rather than potential benefits
3863069.formatting: Separate direct participant benefits from broader scientific or societal benefits. State explicitly if there are no direct benefits. Use measured language ('may,' 'potential') rather than definitive claims.

3863071.name: Data Management and Privacy/Confidentiality (Main Protocol)
3863071.prompt: Provide a comprehensive description of data management and privacy/confidentiality protections. Address how participant privacy will be protected during recruitment, consent, and data collection (e.g., private settings, secure communication). Describe whether data will be identifiable, coded, or de-identified, and detail the coding system if used. Specify all physical and electronic security measures for data storage, including encryption standards, password policies, server locations, and locked storage. Identify all individuals and entities who will have access to identifiable information, and describe the plan and timeline for de-identifying or destroying data after the study.
commonIssues: Addressing only confidentiality (data) while ignoring privacy (persons) protections during study activities
Not specifying whether data is collected as identifiable, coded with a key, or fully de-identified
Failing to describe who holds the code key and where it is stored separately from the data
Omitting specific technical safeguards (e.g., AES-256 encryption, institutional server vs. personal computer)
Not listing all parties with data access, including sponsors, regulatory agencies, or collaborators
Failing to address the minimum necessary standard for identifiable information access
3863071.formatting: Organize into subsections: privacy during study activities, data collection and coding, storage security, access controls, and data disposition timeline. Be specific about technical and administrative safeguards.

3863075.name: Data Analysis (Main Protocol)
3863075.prompt: Describe the complete data analysis plan, including the specific statistical tests or qualitative analysis methods that will be used to address each research question or hypothesis. Specify the analysis software, how data will be cleaned and prepared, and whether analyses will be conducted on identifiable or de-identified datasets. If applicable, describe interim analyses and how they will affect study continuation. Address how results will be reported to prevent the identification of individual participants.
commonIssues: Not aligning the analysis methods with the stated research questions or hypotheses
Providing only vague descriptions such as 'descriptive and inferential statistics' without naming specific tests
Failing to state whether the analysis will use identifiable or de-identified data
Omitting the software or platform that will be used for analysis
Not describing data cleaning procedures or how missing data will be handled
Failing to address how results will be reported to protect participant confidentiality
3863075.formatting: Link each analysis method to its corresponding research question or hypothesis. Specify the software, whether data is identifiable or coded during analysis, and reporting safeguards.

3863076.name: Data Safety Monitoring
3863076.prompt: Describe the data safety monitoring plan for this study, including who will be responsible for monitoring participant safety and data integrity, how frequently monitoring will occur, and what criteria will trigger a review or study modification. For studies involving greater than minimal risk, describe whether a Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) will be used and its composition. Specify the procedures for reporting adverse events, unanticipated problems, and protocol deviations to the IRB, and describe any stopping rules that would lead to early study termination.
commonIssues: Not specifying who is responsible for ongoing safety monitoring and their qualifications
Failing to describe the frequency and methods of safety monitoring reviews
Omitting stopping rules or criteria for early study termination due to safety concerns
Not addressing the process for reporting adverse events and unanticipated problems to the IRB
Failing to justify why a DSMB is or is not needed based on the study risk level
Providing a generic monitoring plan without connecting it to the specific risks of the study
3863076.formatting: Describe the monitoring structure, frequency, responsible parties, adverse event reporting procedures, and stopping rules. For clinical trials or greater-than-minimal-risk studies, address DSMB composition and charter.

3863079.name: Data/Specimens Storage (Main Protocol)
3863079.prompt: Address each of the following: (1) Describe where the data or specimens will be stored (specific location, building, server) and for how long. (2) Explain how the data or specimens will be labeled, including whether identifiers, codes, or de-identified labels will be used. (3) Identify all individuals who will have access to the data or specimens. (4) State whether data or specimens will be shared with other investigators, and if so, describe the data use agreements, de-identification procedures, and safeguards that will govern sharing. Include both physical and electronic storage details.
commonIssues: Not specifying exact storage locations (generic 'secure location' is insufficient)
Failing to state a specific data retention period or providing an indefinite timeline without justification
Not describing the labeling/coding system in sufficient detail
Omitting individuals or entities who may access data (e.g., sponsors, regulatory bodies, collaborators)
Not addressing the conditions, agreements, or safeguards for data sharing with other investigators
Failing to describe the method and timeline for ultimate data or specimen destruction
3863079.formatting: Use a numbered format matching the four required questions. Provide specific details including physical locations, retention periods, labeling methods, access lists, and sharing agreements.
